description: Kaggle historical loader/backfill (build-order step 8) + the src/gammamap pipeline README. Fetch the free CC0 Kaggle dataset (kylegraupe/qqq-daily-option-chains-q1-2020-to-q4-2022), parse it through the source-abstraction layer into the internal schema, run the full engine (surface parity forward -> GEX with volume proxy -> mapping -> levels) to produce per-date levels files for a sample of 2020-2022 QQQ dates, with the volume-proxy flag set on every one. Commit the small distilled per-date levels outputs, NOT the 628MB raw CSV (gitignore it like the CBOE raw chains). This is what lets the user click a replay date and see GEX levels for historical QQQ days. Also write the pipeline README covering live-today and historical-Kaggle-date usage.
steps: Create scripts/backfill_kaggle.py that: downloads the zip from https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/kylegraupe/qqq-daily-option-chains-q1-2020-to-q4-2022 (verified: GET returns 200, ~132MB zip containing qqq_2020_2022.csv, 628MB uncompressed, no auth needed). IMPORTANT sandbox quirk: /tmp does NOT persist between bash calls, so the download+parse must happen in one process run; download into a gitignored path under the repo (e.g. data/kaggle_raw/) which DOES persist. Stream/iterate the CSV rather than loading 628MB into memory at once.

Parse via the FEAT-002 Kaggle adapter (bracketed/space-padded headers). Group rows by QUOTE_DATE; each date is a point-in-time EOD (16:00 EST) chain. For a bounded sample of dates (e.g. one per month, or a documented small set spanning 2020-2022 including a few notable dates), build levels using the engine. Because there is NO OI column, GEX uses the volume proxy and EVERY output must carry proxy=True and the 'oi_absent_volume_proxy' flag; the levels files must be clearly labeled proxy so they are never presented as classic OI-GEX.

Mapping for historical QQQ: the Kaggle data is QQQ-only with UNDERLYING_LAST as spot and no NQ futures quote for those dates. Handle the missing-basis case explicitly: either (a) map QQQ->QQQ-equivalent index and flag basis as unavailable/estimated, or (b) emit the levels in QQQ/NDX-equivalent space with a clear flag that MNQ mapping for historical dates lacks a synchronized NQ basis. Document the choice; never silently fabricate a basis. This is a documented v1 limitation.

Write per-date levels JSON to data/levels/kaggle/<quote_date>_qqq.json, deterministic and small. Add data/kaggle_raw/ (and the raw csv/zip) to .gitignore. Commit the distilled per-date levels files, not the raw.

Create src/gammamap/README.md describing the full pipeline (capture -> source-abstraction -> surface -> gex -> mapping -> levels -> Tradovate indicator) and giving exact commands to produce a levels file for (a) live today (run scripts/capture_snapshot.py then build_levels on the new snapshot) and (b) a historical Kaggle date (run scripts/backfill_kaggle.py). Note the pyenv export + PYTHONPATH=src requirement and the proxy caveat for historical dates.

Add tests/test_backfill.py that runs the Kaggle adapter + engine on a SMALL inline CSV fixture (a handful of rows with the exact bracketed header, not the 628MB file) end-to-end to a levels dict, asserting proxy=True and 'oi_absent_volume_proxy' present and that a wall is selected. Do NOT download the full dataset in the test.
Commit on nuke_root: 'feat: Kaggle historical QQQ backfill (volume-proxy levels) + gammamap pipeline README'.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/backfill_kaggle.py downloads and parses the CC0 dataset via the source-abstraction layer and produces per-date QQQ levels files for a documented sample of 2020-2022 dates.
Every historical levels file carries proxy=True and the 'oi_absent_volume_proxy' flag and is never labeled classic OI-GEX.
The 628MB raw CSV / zip is gitignored (data/kaggle_raw/) and NOT committed; the small per-date levels files ARE committed.
Missing NQ basis for historical dates is handled explicitly and flagged, not fabricated.
src/gammamap/README.md documents producing a levels file for live-today and for a historical Kaggle date, including the pyenv/PYTHONPATH setup.
tests/test_backfill.py runs end-to-end on a small inline fixture (no full download) and passes, asserting the proxy flags.
verification: export PYENV_ROOT="/root/.pyenv" && export PATH="$PYENV_ROOT/shims:$PYENV_ROOT/bin:$PATH" && pyenv global 3.11.15 && PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_backfill.py -q
